cue.target: Chest, with front delts and triceps assisting
setup: Pinch your shoulder blades together and down, lift your chest, and keep them pinned for the whole set.
Grip about one and a half times shoulder width; feet flat, eyes under the bar.
execution: Lower for two to three seconds to your lower chest, elbows tucked about 45 degrees.
Touch softly, then drive the bar up and slightly back toward your face.
Push your feet into the floor as the bar leaves your chest; hips stay down.
cue.feel: A stretch across the whole chest at the bottom, then the pecs squeezing the bar up and back.
cue.mistake: Letting the shoulder blades slide forward or bouncing the bar; both hand the work to the shoulders.
cue.quickCue: Shoulder blades pinned, touch low, press up and back.

cue.target: Upper chest, with front delts and triceps assisting
setup: Set the bench to a low incline, around 30 degrees; steeper hands more work to the shoulders.
Shoulder blades pinched and down, chest up, hands just outside shoulder width.
execution: Lower for two to three seconds to your upper chest, just below the collarbones.
Keep elbows tucked about 45 degrees and under the bar, not flared level with it.
Touch softly and press up and slightly back until the bar is over your shoulders.
cue.feel: A stretch high on the chest near the collarbones at the bottom, and the upper pecs driving the press.
cue.mistake: A steep bench angle or letting the bar drift toward the neck, which turns it into a shoulder press.
cue.quickCue: Low incline, touch just below the collarbones.

cue.target: Mid and lower chest, with triceps and front delts assisting
setup: Hook your legs under the pads first, then lie back and pinch your shoulder blades down.
Use a spotter for the unrack; the decline makes lifting out awkward on your own.
execution: Lower for two to three seconds to the bottom of your chest, elbows tucked about 45 degrees.
The range is shorter than flat, so make every rep touch; no partial reps.
Press up and slightly back until the bar sits over your shoulders.
cue.feel: The lower half of the chest doing the work, with less shoulder involvement than flat or incline.
cue.mistake: Loading it heavy because the short range makes it feel strong, then bouncing the bar off the chest.
cue.quickCue: Short range, so touch every rep under control.

cue.target: Chest, with front delts assisting; less triceps than the barbell
setup: Sit with the dumbbells on your thighs, then lie back and kick them up together.
Shoulder blades pinched and down, feet flat, dumbbells stacked over your shoulders.
execution: Lower for two to three seconds, forearms vertical, until the handles sit just below chest level.
Use the extra depth the dumbbells allow: a deeper stretch than a bar, but no bouncing.
Press up and slightly inward so both dumbbells finish over your shoulders, not clanging together.
cue.feel: A deeper stretch across the chest at the bottom than the barbell gives, then the pecs pulling the arms together.
cue.mistake: Letting the hands drift wider than the elbows, which loses control and shifts the load onto the shoulders.
cue.quickCue: Forearms vertical, stretch deeper than a bar allows.

cue.target: Upper chest, with front delts assisting
setup: Bench at a low incline, around 30 degrees; kick the dumbbells up from your thighs.
Shoulder blades pinched and down, chest up, dumbbells stacked over your shoulders.
execution: Lower for two to three seconds with upper arms about 45 degrees from your torso.
Go deeper than a bar would allow, until you feel a full stretch high on the chest.
Press up and slightly inward, keeping your hands stacked over your elbows the whole way.
cue.feel: A deep stretch across the upper chest at the bottom, then the upper pecs pulling the arms up and together.
cue.mistake: Stopping the descent early or going too heavy to control it; both rob the upper chest of its stretch.
cue.quickCue: Low incline, full stretch, hands over elbows.

cue.target: Chest, with front delts and triceps assisting
setup: Set the seat so the handles line up with mid-chest, just below the shoulders.
Pull the shoulder blades back and down against the pad and plant the feet.
execution: Press the handles forward until the arms are straight, elbows tucked around 45 degrees.
Lower for two to three seconds through the fullest range the machine allows.
Keep the shoulder blades pinned to the pad; do not let the shoulders roll forward at the end.
cue.feel: A deep stretch across the chest at the back of the rep and a strong squeeze at the front.
cue.mistake: Cutting the range short; the machine's stretch position is what makes it worth doing.
cue.quickCue: Blades pinned, full stretch back, press through

cue.target: Chest, with front delts and triceps assisting
setup: Set the bench so the fixed bar path meets your lower chest, not your neck.
Shoulder blades pinched and down, chest up, grip slightly wider than the barbell version.
execution: Unhook, then lower for two to three seconds to a soft touch on your lower chest.
The bar cannot drift, so spend the effort squeezing your chest, not balancing.
Press straight up to lockout; the rails make it safe to push hard without a spotter.
cue.feel: Same chest stretch and squeeze as the barbell, with more attention free for the pecs.
cue.mistake: Bench placed so the bar lands high on the chest or neck, turning it into a shoulder press.
cue.quickCue: Line the bar up with your lower chest first.

cue.target: Lower and mid chest, with triceps and front delts assisting
setup: Grip bars slightly wider than your shoulders, feet tucked behind, shoulders pulled down from your ears.
Lean your torso forward and hold that lean; it is what moves the load onto the chest.
execution: Lower with the elbows drifting out and back until your shoulders dip just below them.
Press back up along the same forward-leaning path, driving through the chest to lockout.
Lower under control for two to three seconds; stop at the same depth every rep.
cue.feel: A strong stretch across the lower chest at the bottom, then the chest squeezing as you press up.
cue.mistake: Drifting upright as you tire, which turns it into a triceps dip and shortens the chest stretch.
cue.quickCue: Lean forward, elbows out, sink into the stretch.

cue.target: Chest, with front delts assisting
setup: Set the pulleys at about shoulder height, take a split stance and step forward.
Lean the torso slightly forward and hold a soft bend in the elbows.
execution: Sweep the handles forward and together in a wide arc, keeping the elbow bend fixed.
Cross the hands at the finish and alternate which hand is on top each set.
Return for two to three seconds and let the arms open wide for the stretch.
cue.feel: Even tension across the chest all the way through; a big stretch out wide and a squeeze in front.
cue.mistake: Letting the cables pull you upright and back; bend forward and fly downward to stay planted.
cue.quickCue: Soft elbows, wide stretch, cross in front
cue.why: A stretch-focused isolation, so it stays light with a long controlled return; a heavy stack just drags the torso around.

cue.target: Chest, with front delts assisting
setup: Set the seat so the handles are level with mid-chest and the pivot with your shoulders.
Sit back, blades against the pad, slight elbow bend, forearms on the pads if it has them.
execution: Bring the handles together in front of the chest in a wide arc.
Squeeze the chest for a beat when the hands meet.
Open for two to three seconds until you feel a strong stretch, without the shoulders rolling forward.
cue.feel: Tension at both ends: a stretch out wide and a squeeze in front, with no dead spot.
cue.mistake: Shrugging or pushing with the hands, which turns it into a front delt move; drive from the elbows.
cue.quickCue: Elbows drive, squeeze together, open slow
cue.why: Isolation on a fixed path; light-to-moderate and strict works best because once the stack gets heavy you stop feeling the chest.

cue.target: Chest, with front delts assisting
setup: Lie on a flat bench, dumbbells over the shoulders, palms facing each other.
Set a slight bend in the elbows and keep it the same for the whole rep.
execution: Lower the dumbbells out in a wide arc until they are about level with the chest.
Bring them back up and together on the same arc, driving from the chest.
Lower for two to three seconds; the bottom stretch is the point of the exercise.
cue.feel: A deep stretch across the chest at the bottom; tension fades near the top where the dumbbells stack over you.
cue.mistake: Turning it into a press by bending the elbows on the way up; keep the arm angle fixed.
cue.quickCue: Fixed elbow bend, deep stretch at the bottom
cue.why: Dumbbells load the chest hardest at the bottom stretch and hardly at the top, so it stays light and strict; the stretch is the work.

cue.target: Upper chest, with front delts assisting
setup: Set a low incline, lie back, and press the dumbbells up over your shoulders, palms facing.
Keep a soft, fixed bend in the elbows and your shoulder blades set back into the bench.
execution: Open your arms in a wide arc until the dumbbells reach about chest level and the pecs stretch.
Hug the weights back up the same arc until they sit over your shoulders, without clanking.
Lower under control for two to three seconds; the stretch at the bottom is the point.
cue.feel: A deep stretch across the upper chest at the bottom that fades as the dumbbells come together.
cue.mistake: Bending the elbows more as you lower, which turns the fly into a press and cuts the stretch.
cue.quickCue: Fixed elbow bend, open wide, stretch the upper chest.
cue.why: Flies are a stretch-focused isolation move with long levers, so a moderate weight you control through the full arc works the chest best.

cue.target: Chest, with front delts and triceps assisting
setup: Hands a little wider than the shoulders and directly under them; feet together, body in one line.
Brace as if about to be punched in the stomach so the hips do not sag.
execution: Lower until the chest touches the floor, elbows tucking to about 45 degrees from the body.
Press back up until the arms are straight, pushing the floor away.
Lower for two to three seconds; the floor stops you before the chest is fully stretched.
cue.feel: Chest working most in the bottom half; the top of the rep is the easy part.
cue.mistake: Hips sagging or piking up; keep a straight line from head to heels.
cue.quickCue: Straight line, chest to floor, push away
cue.why: Bodyweight is hard to add to, so reps run high; slow lowering, a pause at the bottom, or hands on blocks adds difficulty.

cue.target: Chest, with front delts and triceps assisting
setup: Hands on a sturdy bench or box, a little wider than the shoulders; walk the feet back.
Body in one straight line from head to heels, abs lightly braced as if bracing for a punch.
execution: Lower under control until the chest touches the edge, elbows tucking to about 45 degrees.
Press the bench away until the arms are straight, keeping the body rigid the whole way.
A lower surface makes it harder; drop the height as it gets easy before moving to the floor.
cue.feel: Chest and the front of the shoulders working as you press off the edge, triceps finishing the rep.
cue.mistake: Hips sagging or piking up so the body bends; keep the straight line from head to heels.
cue.quickCue: Straight line, chest to the edge, push away
cue.why: Raising the hands takes some bodyweight off, so it is the push-up regression; lower the surface rather than chasing endless reps.

cue.target: Lats and upper back, with biceps and forearms assisting
setup: Grip overhand about one and a half times shoulder width; step off a box, don't jump.
Hang with arms long, squeeze your glutes, and keep the legs still for the whole set.
execution: Start by pulling your shoulder blades down, then drive your elbows down toward your back pockets.
Lift your chest slightly toward the bar and finish with your chin clearly over it every rep.
Lower under control for two to three seconds until your arms are nearly straight again.
cue.feel: Lats stretching hard at the bottom, then squeezing your elbows into your sides on the way up.
cue.mistake: Cutting reps short at either end, or swinging the hips and legs to kick yourself upward.
cue.quickCue: Elbows to back pockets, chin over bar.

cue.target: Lats, with upper back and biceps assisting
setup: Set the thigh pad so heels stay flat; grip overhand, roughly one and a half times shoulder width.
Sit tall, lift your chest, and let your arms go fully straight overhead before each rep.
execution: Pull your shoulder blades down first, then drive the elbows down and in toward your sides.
Touch the bar lightly to your upper chest, leaning back only ten to fifteen degrees.
Lower under control for two to three seconds and let the lats stretch fully at the top.
cue.feel: Lats doing the pulling under your armpits, with a strong stretch as the bar rises.
cue.mistake: Rocking the torso back and yanking with the arms, which hands the work to the lower back.
cue.quickCue: Chest up, elbows down and in, slow negative.

cue.target: Lats, with teres major and biceps assisting
setup: Set the knee pad so the heels stay planted; take the parallel handles, palms facing each other.
Sit tall, lift the chest, and let the arms stretch fully overhead before the first rep.
execution: Drive the elbows down toward the hips, bringing the handle to the upper chest.
Keep the torso close to vertical; a slight lean back is fine if the cable stays straight.
Resist the way up for two to three seconds and feel the lats lengthen at the top.
cue.feel: Lats pulling from the armpits toward the hips, with a big stretch at the top of each rep.
cue.mistake: Yanking with the arms and rocking back, which moves the rep to the biceps and lower back.
cue.quickCue: Elbows down to your hips, stretch at top

cue.target: Lats, with the biceps assisting more than a wide grip
setup: Use the narrow V handle, or hands about shoulder width apart on the bar.
Sit tall with chest lifted; lean the torso back slightly more than on the wide grip.
execution: Drive the elbows down and in front of you, keeping them close to your ribs.
Pull the handle to the top of your chest; think of pulling your elbows toward your hips.
Lower under control for two to three seconds and let the arms reach fully overhead.
cue.feel: A deep stretch down the lats at the top, then the lats along your ribs squeezing.
cue.mistake: Curling with the arms and shrugging up; keep the shoulders down and let the elbows lead.
cue.quickCue: Elbows to hips, arms are just hooks.

cue.target: Whole back: lats, mid traps, rhomboids, rear delts
setup: Hinge at the hips with knees soft until your torso is around 45 degrees or lower.
Grip overhand a little wider than shoulder width; lower back tight, chest up, arms long.
execution: Let the shoulder blades slide forward at the bottom for a full stretch, then row.
Drive elbows up and back at about 45 degrees, touching the bar to your lower ribs or belly.
Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top, then lower under control for two to three seconds.
cue.feel: The whole back stretching wide at the bottom and then bunching together as the bar touches.
cue.mistake: Heaving with the hips or rounding the lower back; hips stay still, only arms and shoulder blades move.
cue.quickCue: Hips still, elbows back, touch the belly.

cue.target: Whole back: lats, mid traps, rear delts; erectors brace
setup: Bar on the floor each rep; torso parallel to the floor, shins vertical, hips pushed back.
Overhand grip a bit wider than shoulders so the forearms are vertical at the top.
execution: From a dead stop, pull the bar hard to your lower sternum, elbows about 45 degrees out.
Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top; the torso should not rise at all.
Lower under control for two to three seconds and let the plates settle fully before the next rep.
cue.feel: Lats stretched hard as the bar rests, then the mid back snapping together at the top.
cue.mistake: Letting the torso rise as the bar comes up; that becomes a hip lift, not a row.
cue.quickCue: Dead stop, torso flat, pull to the sternum.

cue.target: Lats and mid back, with rear delts and biceps assisting
setup: Straddle the bar, feet wider than shoulders, hinge to 45 degrees with lower back tight.
Neutral close handles keep elbows tucked for lats; wide handles flare them for upper back.
execution: Let the arms hang fully at the bottom so the lats and shoulder blades stretch.
Drive the elbows up and back and bring the plates to your chest; torso stays put.
Squeeze the shoulder blades at the top, then lower under control for two to three seconds.
cue.feel: Lats and mid back loading as the weight hangs, then the whole back squeezing at the top.
cue.mistake: Standing up as the weight rises; if the torso climbs past 45 degrees, the load is too heavy.
cue.quickCue: Hinge, hold the angle, elbows up and back.

cue.target: Lats and mid back, with rear delts and biceps assisting
setup: Straddle the bar, feet wider than shoulders, hinge to 45 degrees with lower back tight.
Neutral close handles keep elbows tucked for lats; wide handles flare them for upper back.
execution: Let the arms hang fully at the bottom so the lats and shoulder blades stretch.
Drive the elbows up and back and bring the plates to your chest; torso stays put.
Squeeze the shoulder blades at the top, then lower under control for two to three seconds.
cue.feel: Lats and mid back loading as the weight hangs, then the whole back squeezing at the top.
cue.mistake: Standing up as the weight rises; if the torso climbs past 45 degrees, the load is too heavy.
cue.quickCue: Hinge, hold the angle, elbows up and back.

cue.target: Lats and mid back, with rear delts; lower back rests
setup: Set the bench so your chest rests on it and arms hang fully without touching the floor.
Pin your chest into the pad; with no need to balance, everything goes into the pull.
execution: Let the shoulder blades spread and the arms hang long at the bottom for a full stretch.
Drive the elbows up and back, keeping them close to your body, until the handles reach your ribs.
Hold the top a second with shoulder blades pinched, then lower under control for two to three seconds.
cue.feel: Pure back: a hard stretch across the shoulder blades, then everything between them locking together at the top.
cue.mistake: Lifting the chest off the pad to finish the rep; if you must, the weight is too heavy.
cue.quickCue: Chest glued to the pad, elbows up and back.

cue.target: Lats and mid back, with rear delts and biceps
setup: Feet on the platform, knees slightly bent, sit tall with the chest up.
Use the close neutral handle for lat emphasis; a wider bar shifts work to the upper back.
execution: Reach forward at the start, letting the shoulder blades spread and the lats stretch.
Drive the elbows back along your sides, pulling the handle to your upper belly.
Sit tall at the finish, squeeze the shoulder blades, then lower under control for two to three seconds.
cue.feel: Lats stretching long as the handle travels forward, then the whole back closing as elbows pass your sides.
cue.mistake: Rocking the torso back and forth to move the stack; the pull comes from the arms and shoulder blades.
cue.quickCue: Reach long, then elbows back along your ribs.

cue.target: Lats on the working side, with mid traps and rear delt
setup: Same-side knee and hand on the bench, other foot wide on the floor for a stable base.
Torso nearly parallel to the floor, chest lifted, back flat, head neutral.
execution: Let the dumbbell hang slightly forward and the shoulder blade drop for a full stretch.
Drag the dumbbell back in an arc toward your hip, elbow close to your side.
Lower under control for two to three seconds, letting the shoulder reach fully toward the floor.
cue.feel: A deep stretch down the side of the lat at the bottom, then the elbow driving toward the hip.
cue.mistake: Rowing too upright, or twisting your whole torso to heave the weight instead of pulling it.
cue.quickCue: Stretch it forward, drag it to the hip.

cue.target: Lats and upper back on the working side, with rear delts
setup: Anchor one end of a barbell in a landmine; stand side-on to the loaded end, staggered stance.
Hinge until your torso is near parallel, free forearm on your front thigh, hip nearest the bar higher.
execution: Grip the bar end overhand and let the arm hang so the shoulder blade stretches forward.
Drive the elbow up and back, keeping hips and torso locked in place.
Lower under control for two to three seconds, reaching fully down before the next rep.
cue.feel: A deep stretch through the lat and upper back at the bottom, then a hard squeeze at the top.
cue.mistake: Twisting your torso to heave the bar up, which swaps back work for momentum.
cue.quickCue: Long stretch down, drive the elbow up and back.

Pin your chest into the pad; with no need to balance, everything goes into the pull.

cue.target: Lats, with triceps long head and rear delts assisting
setup: Attach a straight bar or rope high, step back, and hinge slightly forward from the hips.
Arms long overhead with a small fixed elbow bend, shoulders reaching up into a stretch.
execution: Sweep the bar down in an arc toward your thighs, moving only at the shoulders.
Finish with your hands by your thighs and upper arms tight against your sides.
Return for two to three seconds, letting the lats lengthen fully overhead without losing tension.
cue.feel: The lats working down the sides of your back, from a stretch overhead to a squeeze at the hips.
cue.mistake: Bending the elbows to shove the bar down like a triceps pressdown, or rocking your torso.
cue.quickCue: Arms stay long, sweep the bar to your thighs.
cue.why: It isolates the lats without biceps help, so a moderate weight you can move strictly beats heavy reps that turn into a pressdown.

cue.target: Lats and chest, with serratus and triceps assisting
setup: Lie on a bench with your head at the end or just off it, feet planted.
Cup one dumbbell with both hands over your chest, elbows softly bent and held there.
execution: Lower the dumbbell back behind your head in an arc until lats and chest stretch.
Pull it back over your chest along the same arc, keeping the elbow bend unchanged.
Lower under control for two to three seconds; find your range before chasing depth.
cue.feel: A long stretch down the sides of your torso and across the chest when the weight is behind your head.
cue.mistake: Bending and straightening the elbows as you go, which turns it into a triceps extension.
cue.quickCue: Soft elbows, arc it back, feel the stretch.
cue.why: The pullover is a stretch-focused move with a long lever, so a moderate weight you can control deep in the stretch works better than heavy.

cue.target: Upper back, with lats, biceps and rear delts assisting
setup: Lie under a low bar or a sturdy table edge; grip it overhand, slightly wider than shoulder width.
Heels on the floor, body straight from shoulders to heels, glutes and abs tight.
execution: Pull the chest up to the bar or edge, driving the elbows back and squeezing the shoulder blades.
Keep the body rigid as one plank; hips rise with the chest, never trailing behind.
Lower under control to straight arms, letting the shoulder blades spread at the bottom.
cue.feel: Mid and upper back squeezing hard at the top, with the arms helping rather than leading.
cue.mistake: Hips sagging so the body bends in the middle and the chest never reaches the bar.
cue.quickCue: Body like a plank, chest to the bar
cue.why: A more upright body makes it easier, feet raised makes it harder; adjust the angle instead of cutting range.

cue.target: Upper back, with lats, biceps and rear delts assisting
setup: Sit on the floor, legs out, knees slightly bent, band looped around the soles of your feet.
Hold one end in each hand, sit tall with a neutral spine, shoulders relaxed.
execution: Pull the hands to the lower ribs, elbows close to the body, squeezing the shoulder blades together.
Keep the torso still; the arms and shoulder blades move, not the lower back.
Return slowly to straight arms, resisting the band rather than letting it snap you forward.
cue.feel: Squeeze between the shoulder blades at the finish, with the lats working as elbows pass the ribs.
cue.mistake: Leaning back to stretch the band moves the work from the back to the hips and lower back.
cue.quickCue: Sit tall, elbows to the ribs, slow return
cue.why: Bands get harder as they stretch, so the finish is the hard part; choke up or use a thicker band to progress.

cue.target: Lats, with biceps assisting
setup: Anchor the band high, such as a door anchor at the top of a closed door.
Kneel or sit facing it, arms reaching up toward the anchor, slightly wider than shoulders.
execution: Pull the shoulder blades down, then drive the elbows down to your sides toward the upper chest.
Chest up and abs braced; the torso stays still rather than leaning back.
Let the arms rise back toward the anchor slowly, feeling the lats stretch at the top.
cue.feel: Lats pulling the elbows down along your sides, with a stretch under the arms on the way up.
cue.mistake: Yanking with the arms or rocking the torso instead of driving the elbows down to the sides.
cue.quickCue: Shoulders down, elbows to your sides

cue.target: Front delts, with side delts, upper chest and triceps assisting
setup: Grip just outside shoulder width, bar resting on your upper chest, elbows slightly ahead of the bar.
Feet under hips, squeeze glutes and abs hard, take a big breath before you press.
execution: Tip your head back slightly, press straight up, then push your head through once the bar passes.
Finish with the bar stacked over your shoulders and mid-foot, then shrug tall at the top.
Lower under control for two to three seconds back to the upper chest.
cue.feel: Front delts and upper chest working hardest off the chest; triceps take over near lockout.
cue.mistake: Leaning back and pushing the bar forward around your face, which turns it into an incline press.
cue.quickCue: Press straight up, then push your head through.

cue.target: Front delts, with side delts and triceps assisting
setup: Bench set upright, bar racked just below shoulder height so you can unrack without reaching.
Grip just outside shoulder width, upper back and hips pressed into the pad, feet planted.
execution: Unrack to your upper chest, then press straight up, tipping your head back to clear the bar.
Lock out with the bar over your shoulders, not out in front of your face.
Lower under control for two to three seconds to the upper chest or collarbones.
cue.feel: Front delts doing the work with no help from your legs; heavier loads, less balancing than standing.
cue.mistake: Sliding your hips forward and arching off the pad, which turns the seated press into an incline press.
cue.quickCue: Back into the pad, bar straight up.

cue.target: Front and side delts, with triceps assisting
setup: Bench upright or one notch back, dumbbells kicked up to shoulder height with your knees.
Upper back on the pad, feet flat, palms forward, wrists stacked over elbows.
execution: Press up and slightly inward until arms are straight above your shoulders.
Keep your back on the pad; the seat, not your lower back, provides the stability.
Lower under control for two to three seconds until the dumbbells reach shoulder height.
cue.feel: Front delts loaded through a deep bottom stretch; more weight than standing because nothing needs balancing.
cue.mistake: Sliding your hips forward so you lean far back, which turns it into an incline chest press.
cue.quickCue: Back on the pad, dumbbells to shoulder height.

cue.target: Front delts, with side delts and triceps assisting
setup: Set the seat so the handles start at about shoulder height, roughly level with the collarbones.
Sit tall, back on the pad, feet flat, wrists stacked over the elbows.
execution: Press up until the arms are straight without slamming the elbows into lockout.
Lower for two to three seconds all the way to shoulder height for the full stretch.
Keep the elbows under the handles throughout so the shoulders stay stacked.
cue.feel: A deep stretch across the front of the shoulder at the bottom, then a strong drive up.
cue.mistake: Stopping the lowering phase short; the bottom stretch is where the machine earns its keep.
cue.quickCue: All the way down to shoulder height, drive up

cue.target: Front delts, with side delts and triceps assisting
setup: Sit on a bench with back support, dumbbells at shoulder height, palms facing you.
Elbows in front of the body, forearms vertical, wrists straight.
execution: Press up while turning the palms outward, so the elbows travel out to the sides as you rise.
Finish with the arms straight overhead, palms facing forward.
Reverse the turn on the way down for two to three seconds, back to palms facing you.
cue.feel: The front delt loads through a longer arc than a plain press because the elbows start in front.
cue.mistake: Shortening the bottom: bring the dumbbells back to shoulder height every rep; the rotation is not a shortcut.
cue.quickCue: Rotate as you press, elbows sweep out

cue.target: Side delts, with upper traps assisting
setup: Stand tall, dumbbells at your sides, palms in, a soft bend in each elbow.
Leaning the torso away from a rack while raising one arm loads the delt sooner.
execution: Lead with the elbows and raise both arms out to the side until level with the shoulders.
Keep wrists in line with elbows; do not let the hands rise above them.
Lower under control for two to three seconds; tension peaks at the top, so own it.
cue.feel: A burn along the outer shoulder that is strongest near the top, where dumbbells load the delt hardest.
cue.mistake: Swinging from the hips or shrugging the weights up shifts the work to the traps and momentum.
cue.quickCue: Elbows lead, raise to shoulder height, lower slow
cue.why: Side delts are small and easy to cheat with a hip swing, so keep it light and strict; only delt-driven reps count.

cue.target: Side delts, one arm at a time, with upper traps assisting
setup: Set the pulley at about hand height, stand side-on, and grab the handle with the far hand.
Start with the handle across your body in front of the hips for a full stretch.
execution: Raise the arm out to the side, leading with the elbow, until roughly shoulder height.
Keep a soft elbow and do not turn the hand as you lift.
Lower for two to three seconds and let the cable pull the arm back across your body.
cue.feel: Even tension the whole way, including the bottom where a dumbbell gives nothing; a steady side delt burn.
cue.mistake: Shrugging or leaning into the stack turns it into a trap exercise; let the delt do the pull.
cue.quickCue: Cable at hand height, sweep out from across your body
cue.why: Cables keep tension on the delt at the bottom, so light strict reps stretch and load it the whole way; heavier just invites shrugging.

cue.target: Side delts, with upper traps assisting
setup: Set the seat so the pads sit just above the elbows and the pivot matches your shoulders.
Sit tall and drive the pads with your upper arms, not your hands.
execution: Raise the elbows out to the side until the upper arms are level with the floor.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower for two to three seconds without letting the stack touch.
Keep the torso still; no leaning back or rocking to start the rep.
cue.feel: Smooth, even tension across the whole range with no dead spot; the machine keeps loading the delt at the bottom.
cue.mistake: Loading it heavy and heaving with the torso; the short lever means small weight jumps feel big.
cue.quickCue: Drive the pads with your elbows, torso still
cue.why: The machine holds tension at the bottom that dumbbells lose, so moderate strict reps and slow lowering do the work; no momentum needed.

cue.target: Front delts, with upper chest assisting
setup: Stand tall, dumbbells in front of your thighs, palms facing down or facing each other.
Soft bend in the elbows, chest proud, ribs down so the torso stays still.
execution: Raise the dumbbells forward to about shoulder height, leading with the hands.
Keep shoulders down; stop at shoulder level rather than shrugging higher.
Lower under control for two to three seconds without swinging into the next rep.
cue.feel: A burn at the front of the shoulder that builds as your arms approach level.
cue.mistake: Leaning back and swinging the weights up with your hips, which hands the rep to momentum.
cue.quickCue: Chest proud, raise to shoulder height, lower slow.
cue.why: Front delts already work hard in pressing, so raises are extra volume; a moderate, strict weight keeps the delt working instead of your hips.

cue.target: Rear delts, with mid traps and rhomboids assisting
setup: Set both pulleys around head height and hold each cable with the opposite hand, arms crossed.
Hold the cable ends themselves, not handles, so the arms can cross without clanging.
execution: Sweep the arms out and back in a wide arc, slight elbow bend, until they are level.
Think about pushing the hands apart rather than yanking them back.
Return for two to three seconds and let the arms cross deeply in front for the stretch.
cue.feel: A deep stretch across the back of the shoulders as the arms cross, then a burn behind the shoulder.
cue.mistake: Pinching the shoulder blades hard together lets the mid traps take over; keep the blades quiet, sweep with the arms.
cue.quickCue: Sweep the cables out, don't yank them back
cue.why: Rear delts are small and the traps happily steal the rep, so this stays light with higher reps and a long stretch, never heaved.

cue.target: Rear delts, with mid traps and rhomboids assisting
setup: Set the seat so the handles sit at shoulder height with your chest against the pad.
Grip the handles with palms facing in and a slight bend in the elbows.
execution: Sweep the arms out and back in a wide arc until they are in line with the torso.
Keep the elbows slightly bent and the hands level with the shoulders the whole way.
Lower for two to three seconds and let the hands come well past the start for the stretch.
cue.feel: Constant tension behind the shoulder; the chest pad means all the load lands on the rear delts.
cue.mistake: Pulling the shoulder blades together and leaning off the pad; that hands the rep to the traps.
cue.quickCue: Chest on the pad, sweep the handles wide
cue.why: The pad locks the torso, so the rear delt gets every bit of the load; keep it light and strict with a full sweep.

cue.target: Rear delts and mid traps, with rotator cuff assisting
setup: Set a rope at about face height or a little lower; stand or kneel in a split stance.
Grab the rope underhand, thumbs toward you, so the shoulders can rotate freely.
execution: Pull the rope toward the face with elbows high and wide, splitting the ends apart.
Finish with the knuckles beside the ears, like a rear double-biceps pose.
Return for two to three seconds and let the shoulder blades glide apart for the stretch.
cue.feel: The back of the shoulders and between the blades work; the cable should stretch the rear delts at the front.
cue.mistake: Loading it heavy and rocking the torso; the cable pulls you forward and the delts lose the rep.
cue.quickCue: Elbows high, pull rope apart, knuckles by ears
cue.why: Light and strict: the rear delts are the small link, and going heavy just hands the rep to the traps and torso swing.

cue.target: Rear delts, with mid traps assisting
setup: Hinge at the hips until the torso is nearly parallel to the floor, back flat.
Let the dumbbells hang under the shoulders, palms facing each other, elbows slightly bent.
execution: Raise the arms out to the sides, leading with the elbows, until level with the torso.
Pause briefly at the top; that squeeze is where the rear delt does its work.
Lower under control for two to three seconds; the bottom half carries little tension.
cue.feel: A short, sharp squeeze behind the shoulder at the top; little tension at the bottom of the rep.
cue.mistake: Bouncing the torso up to swing the weights; keep the hips still and let the delts lift.
cue.quickCue: Torso still, elbows out, pause at the top
cue.why: Dumbbells give the rear delt almost no load at the bottom, so this stays light and strict with a pause at the top.

cue.target: Front delts, with triceps and side delts assisting
setup: From a high plank, hands about shoulder width, walk the feet in and lift the hips high.
Body forms an upside-down V; legs as straight as your hamstrings allow, neck neutral.
execution: Bend the elbows and lower the head forward and down to a spot just ahead of the hands.
Keep elbows tucked toward the body rather than flared straight out to the sides.
Press back up to straight arms under control, keeping the hips high throughout.
cue.feel: Shoulders doing the pressing, like an overhead press, with the triceps finishing at the top.
cue.mistake: Letting the hips drop toward a plank turns it back into a regular push-up and off the shoulders.
cue.quickCue: Hips high, head forward of the hands, press
cue.why: It is the bodyweight overhead press; raising the feet onto a box makes it more vertical and harder.

cue.target: Rear delts, with the upper back assisting
setup: Stand tall holding a light band in front at shoulder height, arms straight, hands about shoulder width.
execution: Pull the band apart by moving the arms out to the sides until it touches the chest.
Keep arms straight and shoulders down; the movement is out to the sides, not down.
Return under control to the start rather than letting the band snap back.
cue.feel: The backs of the shoulders and between the shoulder blades working as the band reaches your chest.
cue.mistake: Bending the elbows or shrugging, which turns it into a row and moves work off the rear delts.
cue.quickCue: Straight arms, pull apart to the chest
cue.why: Rear delts are small, so a light band with strict form works better than a heavy band you cannot finish.

cue.target: Upper traps, with forearms working to hold the bar
setup: Hold the bar overhand, hands just outside your thighs or a little wider, standing tall.
Arms hang straight like ropes; the hands only hold the bar, they do not lift it.
execution: Shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears, slightly back, without rolling them.
Hold the top for a moment and squeeze before you lower.
Lower under control for two to three seconds into a full stretch at the bottom.
cue.feel: The tops of your shoulders bunching up hard beside the neck, then a stretch as they drop.
cue.mistake: Loading so heavy that you dip your chin toward your shoulders instead of lifting the shoulders.
cue.quickCue: Shoulders to ears, pause, drop into a full stretch.
cue.why: The barbell loads heavy easily, but traps respond to full range and a pause; weight that cuts the shrug short just moves your head.

cue.target: Upper traps, with forearms working to hold the weights
setup: Stand tall with a dumbbell at each side, palms facing in, arms hanging straight.
Keep the dumbbells beside your hips, not in front, so the shoulders rise freely.
execution: Shrug straight up toward your ears, letting the dumbbells travel straight up your sides.
Pause and squeeze at the top without bending the elbows.
Lower under control for two to three seconds and let the shoulders sink fully.
cue.feel: Traps squeezing hard beside the neck at the top and stretching down the sides at the bottom.
cue.mistake: Rolling the shoulders in circles or bending the elbows, which adds nothing for the traps.
cue.quickCue: Weights at your sides, straight up, pause, sink.
cue.why: Dumbbells suit lighter, higher-rep shrugs than a barbell; the neutral grip lets you chase a full range and a clean pause.

cue.target: Upper traps, under steady cable tension
setup: Face a low pulley with a straight bar, or stand between two low pulleys holding handles.
Stand close to the pulley so the cable runs nearly straight down, shoulders relaxed into a stretch.
execution: Shrug straight up toward your ears, arms long and torso tall.
Hold the top for a moment; the cable keeps the traps loaded there.
Lower under control for two to three seconds, letting the cable stretch the traps fully.
cue.feel: Constant tension through the upper traps, a hard squeeze at the top and a pull into the stretch.
cue.mistake: Bending the elbows or rolling the shoulders instead of lifting them straight up and down.
cue.quickCue: Tall torso, shoulders to ears, pause, full stretch.
cue.why: Cables keep tension through the whole shrug and suit lighter, higher-rep work better than heavy loading.

cue.target: Biceps, with brachialis and forearms assisting
setup: Stand tall, shoulder-width underhand grip, bar hanging at arm's length with elbows at your sides.
Brace your abs and keep the chest up so the torso cannot rock.
execution: Curl the bar up until your forearms are vertical, elbows pinned to your sides.
Do not let the elbows lift forward as the bar rises; that shortens the biceps.
Lower under control for two to three seconds all the way to straight arms.
cue.feel: Biceps stretching hard at the bottom and squeezing at the top, with both arms working equally.
cue.mistake: Swinging the hips and shoulders to start the rep, which uses momentum instead of the biceps.
cue.quickCue: Elbows pinned, full stretch at the bottom.

cue.target: Biceps, with brachialis and forearms assisting
setup: Grip the angled sections so palms are half turned up and your wrists sit at a natural angle.
Stand tall, elbows at your sides, abs braced.
execution: Curl until forearms are vertical with elbows pinned to your sides.
Choose the inner or outer angles for a narrower or wider grip; both hit the biceps.
Lower under control for two to three seconds to fully straight arms.
cue.feel: Same biceps stretch and squeeze as the straight bar, with less wrist twist so heavier loads feel comfortable.
cue.mistake: Rocking the torso and letting the elbows swing forward, which turns it into a front raise.
cue.quickCue: Elbows pinned, full range, no body swing.

cue.target: Biceps, with brachialis and forearms assisting
setup: Dumbbells at your sides, palms facing in, arms straight, elbows tucked against your ribs.
Stand tall with abs braced; alternate arms or curl both together.
execution: Curl and turn the palm up as the dumbbell rises, finishing with the pinky slightly higher.
Keep the elbow still at your side; only the forearm moves.
Lower under control for two to three seconds, turning the palm back in near the bottom.
cue.feel: Biceps tightening as you twist the palm up; a stretch through the front of the arm at the bottom.
cue.mistake: Driving the elbow forward to help the weight up, which lets the front delt take over.
cue.quickCue: Turn the palm up as you curl.

cue.target: Biceps, long head emphasised
setup: Set the bench to a moderate incline and sit back fully, shoulders against the pad.
Let the arms hang straight down and slightly behind your torso, palms forward.
execution: Curl by driving the pinky side of the hand up, keeping the upper arm hanging still.
Squeeze at the top, then lower for two to three seconds to a fully straight arm.
Go all the way down every rep; the stretched bottom is the point of this variant.
cue.feel: A pronounced stretch through the biceps at the bottom, with the squeeze building as you curl.
cue.mistake: Letting the elbows drift forward as you tire, which removes the stretch this exercise exists for.
cue.quickCue: Arms hang back; stretch fully at the bottom.
cue.why: Loaded light: the arms-behind-the-body position stretches the biceps under load, and that lengthened work drives growth; heaving forward destroys the stretch.

exercises.name: Preacher Curl
exercises.equipment: Preacher Bench, Barbell or EZ Bar

cue.target: Biceps, with brachialis assisting
setup: Set the pad so your armpits sit at its top edge and the upper arms lie flat.
Grip the bar or dumbbell shoulder-width, palms up, chest against the pad.
execution: Curl up until the forearm is vertical, driving through the pinky side to keep the palm turned up.
Lower for two to three seconds all the way to nearly straight, never bouncing off the pad.
cue.feel: Heaviest at the bottom, with the biceps loaded hard while stretched; the top is easy by comparison.
cue.mistake: Cutting the bottom short. The stretched bottom is where the tension is; half reps waste the exercise.
cue.quickCue: All the way down, no bounce, pinky drives up.
cue.why: Strict by design: the pad locks the upper arm so cheating is impossible, and the angle loads the biceps hardest in the stretched bottom position.

exercises.name: Cable Curl
exercises.equipment: Cable Machine, Straight Bar or EZ Bar

cue.target: Biceps, with brachialis and forearms assisting
setup: Low pulley with a bar attachment; step back until the cable is taut with straight arms.
Elbows at your sides, chest up, abs braced.
execution: Curl until forearms are vertical, keeping elbows still; the cable keeps tension on at the bottom.
Do not step in or lean back; that slackens the cable exactly where free weights go slack.
Lower under control for two to three seconds until arms are fully straight.
cue.feel: Constant tension through the whole rep, including a loaded stretch at the bottom that dumbbells cannot give.
cue.mistake: Letting the weight pull your elbows forward, lining the cable up with your forearm and unloading the biceps.
cue.quickCue: Elbows still, stay back, keep the cable tight.

cue.target: Brachialis and brachioradialis, with biceps assisting
setup: Dumbbells at your sides, palms facing your thighs, thumbs pointing forward.
Stand tall, elbows tucked at your ribs, abs braced.
execution: Curl with the thumb leading until the thumb reaches shoulder height and the forearm is vertical.
Keep the palms facing each other the entire rep; no turning the wrist.
Lower under control for two to three seconds to straight arms.
cue.feel: Work sitting deeper and lower in the upper arm than a normal curl, plus the top of the forearm.
cue.mistake: Rotating the palm up or swinging the elbow forward, which turns it back into a biceps curl.
cue.quickCue: Thumbs up, palms in, elbows still.

cue.target: Brachialis and brachioradialis, with biceps assisting
setup: Dumbbells at your sides, palms facing your thighs, thumbs pointing forward.
Stand tall, elbows tucked at your ribs, abs braced.
execution: Curl with the thumb leading until the thumb reaches shoulder height and the forearm is vertical.
Keep the palms facing each other the entire rep; no turning the wrist.
Lower under control for two to three seconds to straight arms.
cue.feel: Work sitting deeper and lower in the upper arm than a normal curl, plus the top of the forearm.
cue.mistake: Rotating the palm up or swinging the elbow forward, which turns it back into a biceps curl.
cue.quickCue: Thumbs up, palms in, elbows still.

cue.target: Biceps, with brachialis assisting
setup: Sit on a bench, feet wide, and brace the back of the upper arm against your inner thigh.
Let the arm hang fully straight with the palm turned up.
execution: Curl toward the shoulder, driving the pinky side of the hand up so the palm stays turned up.
Squeeze hard at the top, then lower for two to three seconds to a straight arm.
The braced upper arm must not move; only the forearm travels.
cue.feel: Nothing but the biceps working; the brace makes it obvious when anything else joins in.
cue.mistake: Rocking the torso or letting the upper arm slide on the thigh to help the weight up.
cue.quickCue: Upper arm braced still, palm up, squeeze the top.
cue.why: Light and strict: with the arm braced there is nowhere to cheat, so the exercise is for a clean squeeze, not big weights.

cue.target: Brachioradialis and brachialis, with biceps assisting
setup: Stand tall, elbows tucked at your sides, holding an EZ bar or barbell palms down.
Use a thumbless grip and clamp the fingers hard into the base of the hand.
execution: Curl to full elbow bend without the elbows drifting forward.
Lower for two to three seconds, keeping the wrist straight or very slightly bent.
Keep the elbows pinned; the forearm does all the travel.
cue.feel: The top of the forearm near the elbow works hardest, especially through the upper half of the curl.
cue.mistake: Letting the bar rest on the thumbs and swinging it up, which takes the forearm out of the lift.
cue.quickCue: Palms down, grip hard, elbows pinned, no swing.
cue.why: Light by nature: with the palm turned down the biceps lose their advantage, so a smaller forearm muscle does the work and loads must drop.

cue.target: Triceps, all three heads; lateral and medial heads emphasised
setup: Set the cable so the bar hangs about eye level; take an overhand, shoulder-width grip.
Pin the elbows to your sides, step back a little, and hinge slightly forward at the hips.
execution: Squeeze the triceps to press the bar down until the elbows are fully straight.
Let the bar rise under control for two to three seconds until forearm meets biceps.
Elbows may drift back an inch as you press, but never forward or out.
cue.feel: Tension stays on the back of the arm the whole rep, with a hard squeeze at lockout.
cue.mistake: Leaning over the bar and pressing with chest and shoulders; the weight moves but the triceps stop working.
cue.quickCue: Elbows pinned, press to full lockout, control the rise.
cue.why: Loaded moderately and strictly: the moment you heave, chest and front delts take over and the triceps lose tension despite a bigger number.

cue.target: Triceps, all three heads
setup: Same cable setup as the bar; hold the rope thumbs up, knuckles down, elbows pinned at your sides.
execution: Press down and, near the bottom, pull the rope ends apart for a harder squeeze.
Return under control for two to three seconds without letting the elbows lift or drift.
cue.feel: Same triceps tension as the bar, with a sharper contraction at the bottom from spreading the rope.
cue.mistake: Loading the rope like the bar; it is less stable, so form collapses and the forearms fight the handles.
cue.quickCue: Spread the rope at the bottom, elbows still.
cue.why: The rope is less stable than a bar, so it takes lighter loads; use it for a strong, deliberate squeeze rather than chasing weight.

cue.target: Triceps, long head especially
setup: Face away from a low or mid pulley, arms overhead, elbows pointing forward beside your ears.
Stagger the feet and lean slightly forward so the cable pulls the arms back into a stretch.
execution: Let the hands travel behind your head until you feel a deep stretch in the triceps.
Extend the elbows to straight without letting them flare or the upper arms drop forward.
Lower back into the stretch under control for two to three seconds every rep.
cue.feel: A strong stretch along the back of the upper arm at the bottom, tension throughout the rep.
cue.mistake: Letting the elbows drop and flare as you tire, which turns it into a press and unloads the long head.
cue.quickCue: Arms stay up; sink into the stretch behind the head.
cue.why: The long head crosses the shoulder, so arms overhead stretch it under load; that stretched, loaded position is why this beats a pushdown for growth.

cue.target: Triceps, especially the long head
setup: Hold a dumbbell, EZ bar or rope overhead; for a dumbbell, cup the top plate with both hands.
Upper arms pointing straight up beside your ears; brace and stand or sit tall.
execution: Bend only at the elbows, lowering the weight behind your head as far as you can.
Extend back to straight arms, keeping the upper arms fixed in place, not swinging forward.
Lower under control for two to three seconds and pause briefly in the stretched position.
cue.feel: A deep stretch down the back of the arm at the bottom, then the triceps driving the extension.
cue.mistake: Letting the elbows drift forward and flare, which turns it into a partial press and unloads the stretch.
cue.quickCue: Upper arms fixed by your ears, deep stretch.

cue.target: Triceps, long head emphasised
setup: Lie on a bench, head just past the end, shoulder blades pulled back and down.
Shoulder-width grip on the angled handles; the EZ bar is easier on the wrists than a straight bar.
execution: Start with the bar slightly behind your head, then lower it in an arc past your face.
Take two to three seconds down until forearms touch biceps.
Drive the bar up and a little forward with the triceps; upper arms stay fixed.
cue.feel: A deep stretch behind the upper arm at the bottom, with tension kept on even at the top.
cue.mistake: Dropping the bar straight to the forehead, which shortens the lever and drops tension on the triceps.
cue.quickCue: Arc the bar behind your head, elbows tucked.
cue.why: Moderate load, strict path: the bar lets you add small weight increments week to week, so progress comes from steady loading, not heaving.

cue.target: Triceps, long head emphasised
setup: Lie on a bench with head near the end, shoulder blades pulled back and down, dumbbells overhead.
Each arm works on its own, so turn the palms slightly in if that sits better.
execution: Bend the elbows and lower the dumbbells in an arc past your head, not to your forehead.
Take two to three seconds down; forearm should touch biceps at the bottom.
Squeeze the triceps to bring the weight up and slightly forward, upper arms staying still.
cue.feel: A deep stretch behind the upper arm at the bottom and tension that never fully drops at the top.
cue.mistake: Letting the upper arms swing toward the feet as you press, which pulls in lats and chest.
cue.quickCue: Arc the weight behind your head, upper arms still.
cue.why: Dumbbells are harder to steady overhead, so keep the load moderate and every rep identical; the stretch matters more than the weight.

cue.target: Triceps, with chest and front delts sharing the load
setup: Hands about shoulder width, no narrower; the same pinned shoulder blades and chest-up setup as the bench.
Feet flat, wrists straight and stacked over the elbows, bar low in the palm.
execution: Lower for two to three seconds with elbows tucked closer than usual, touching lower on the chest.
The narrow grip adds range, so let the bar travel all the way down before pressing.
Drive up and slightly back, straightening the elbows hard to a full lockout.
cue.feel: The back of the arms working hardest, especially in the last third to lockout; chest still assists.
cue.mistake: Gripping so narrow the wrists bend back and the elbows flare out; that hands the work back to the chest.
cue.quickCue: Shoulder-width grip, elbows tucked, lock out hard.

cue.target: Triceps, with front delts and lower chest assisting
setup: Grip the bars at shoulder width, arms locked, torso tall and nearly vertical, legs under you.
Pull shoulders down and back; keep elbows pointing straight back, not out.
execution: Bend the elbows straight back, staying upright, until upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
Press through the palms to a full, hard lockout at the top.
Lower under control for two to three seconds; same depth every rep.
cue.feel: The back of the arms doing most of the work, strongest as you push through lockout; chest only lightly stretched.
cue.mistake: Letting the torso pitch forward and elbows flare as you tire, which turns it back into a chest dip.
cue.quickCue: Stay upright, elbows back, lock out hard.

cue.target: Triceps, especially the long head, fully shortened behind the body
setup: Hinge forward until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor, free hand braced on a bench.
Lift the upper arm so it sits alongside or slightly behind your torso, elbow bent.
execution: Straighten the elbow until the arm is fully locked out behind you; squeeze there briefly.
Upper arm stays still; only the forearm moves.
Lower under control for two to three seconds back to a right angle at the elbow.
cue.feel: A hard, crampy squeeze in the back of the upper arm at lockout, with little tension at the bottom.
cue.mistake: Letting the upper arm drop and swing, so momentum and the shoulder move the weight instead of the triceps.
cue.quickCue: Pin the upper arm high, lock out behind you.
cue.why: Kept light and strict: the triceps are fully shortened at lockout, so heavy dumbbells just get swung and the squeeze is lost.

cue.target: Triceps, with chest and front delts assisting
setup: Hands under your shoulders or slightly narrower, fingers forward, body straight from head to heels.
Squeeze glutes and brace your abs as if about to be punched.
execution: Lower your chest to the floor with elbows tucked close, brushing your ribs.
Push the floor away until elbows lock; hips and shoulders rise as one unit.
Lower under control for two to three seconds, then press all the way up.
cue.feel: Triceps taking more of the push than a normal push-up, especially through the last half of lockout.
cue.mistake: Letting the elbows flare out wide, which hands the work back to the chest and shoulders.
cue.quickCue: Elbows tucked, chest to the floor, full lockout.

cue.target: Triceps, with chest and front delts assisting
setup: Thumbs and index fingers touch under your chest in a diamond; body straight, glutes squeezed.
Narrower than a close-grip push-up, so expect fewer reps and more triceps demand.
execution: Lower until your chest touches your hands, elbows tracking back along your ribs.
Press to full lockout and squeeze the triceps hard at the top.
Lower under control for two to three seconds every rep.
cue.feel: Triceps working through the whole rep with a strong squeeze at lockout; inner chest joins near the top.
cue.mistake: Flaring the elbows out to the sides, which shifts the load to the chest and shoulders.
cue.quickCue: Hands in a diamond, elbows back, lock out hard.

cue.target: Quads and glutes, with adductors and lower back holding position
setup: Bar high on the traps, hands close, elbows pointed back; stand feet wider than shoulders, toes out.
Big breath into the belly, brace hard, weight spread across heel and both sides of the forefoot.
execution: Bend knees and hips together, knees tracking over your toes, bar traveling straight down over midfoot.
Lower under control to at least parallel, then drive your upper back into the bar and stand.
Keep your chest from tipping forward as you rise; hips and shoulders come up at the same speed.
cue.feel: Quads loaded hardest at the bottom, glutes taking over through the middle; the trunk stays rigid throughout.
cue.mistake: Hips shooting up first tips you forward and moves the load from your quads onto your lower back.
cue.quickCue: Sit down between your knees, drive back into the bar.

cue.target: Quads, more than the back squat, with upper back holding you upright
setup: Bar sits on the front of the shoulders against the neck, fingertips under it, elbows driven high.
Crossed arms or straps are fine if the rack feels awkward; upper arms stay parallel to the floor.
execution: Brace, then sit straight down, not back; knees travel forward and out further than a back squat.
Lower under control to below parallel, torso nearly vertical, elbows still pointing straight ahead.
Drive up leading with chest and elbows, pushing the hips forward under the bar.
cue.feel: Quads working hard from the bottom up, with your upper back straining to keep you tall.
cue.mistake: Elbows dropping as you tire lets the chest fall and the bar roll forward, ending the rep early.
cue.quickCue: Elbows high, sit straight down, stand tall.

cue.target: Quads and glutes, with adductors and lower back holding position
setup: Bar high on the traps, hands close, elbows pointed back; stand feet wider than shoulders, toes out.
Big breath into the belly, brace hard, weight spread across heel and both sides of the forefoot.
execution: Bend knees and hips together, knees tracking over your toes, bar traveling straight down over midfoot.
Lower under control to at least parallel, then drive your upper back into the bar and stand.
Keep your chest from tipping forward as you rise; hips and shoulders come up at the same speed.
cue.feel: Quads loaded hardest at the bottom, glutes taking over through the middle; the trunk stays rigid throughout.
cue.mistake: Hips shooting up first tips you forward and moves the load from your quads onto your lower back.
cue.quickCue: Sit down between your knees, drive back into the bar.

cue.target: Quads, with glutes assisting
setup: Bar across the upper back, feet shoulder width and a little in front of the bar path.
Placing the feet slightly forward lets the torso stay upright, which keeps the work on the quads.
execution: Brace as if about to be punched in the stomach, then break at the knees and hips together.
Squat as deep as you can with the heels down and knees tracking over the toes.
Lower under control for two to three seconds, then drive the whole foot into the floor.
cue.feel: Quads stretching at the bottom and taking the load up; the fixed bar means you push straight down.
cue.mistake: Standing directly under the bar and folding forward turns it into a lower back and hip exercise.
cue.quickCue: Feet slightly forward, torso tall, go deep.

cue.target: Quads, with glutes assisting
setup: Back and hips flat on the pad, shoulders under the pads, feet shoulder width mid platform.
Toes slightly out; keeping the feet lower on the platform keeps the work on the quads.
execution: Unlock the safeties and lower until the thighs pass parallel, or as deep as you can control.
Keep the whole foot pressed into the platform and the knees tracking over the toes.
Lower under control for two to three seconds, then drive up without locking the knees.
cue.feel: A deep stretch across the front of the thighs at the bottom, quads working the whole way up.
cue.mistake: Heels lifting or the lower back peeling off the pad at the bottom shifts load away from the quads.
cue.quickCue: Deep, heels down, knees over toes.

cue.target: Quads, with glutes and adductors assisting
setup: Sit with the lower back and hips pressed into the pad; feet flat, shoulder width, toes slightly out.
Place the feet low to mid platform for quads; higher foot placement shifts work to hips and hamstrings.
execution: Lower the sled as deep as you can while the lower back stays glued to the pad.
Push through the whole foot, keeping the knees in line with the toes.
Lower under control for two to three seconds and stop just short of locking the knees.
cue.feel: Quads loading hard through the bottom half; the hips stay planted rather than rolling up.
cue.mistake: Going so deep that the hips and lower back curl off the pad, moving the load off the quads.
cue.quickCue: Deep as your back stays flat.

cue.target: Quads, with glutes assisting
setup: Back flat on the pad, shoulders under the pads, feet mid platform about shoulder width.
The platform swings in an arc, so let the knees travel forward rather than sitting back.
execution: Lower as deep as you can while the hips and back stay on the pad.
Keep the whole foot planted and the knees tracking over the toes.
Lower under control for two to three seconds, then drive up without locking the knees.
cue.feel: A strong quad stretch at the bottom that gets heavier as you go down, then quads driving up.
cue.mistake: Hips lifting off the pad at the bottom to reach depth, which takes tension off the quads.
cue.quickCue: Knees forward, back on the pad, go deep.

cue.target: Front-leg quads and glutes, with the outer hip stabilising
setup: Rear foot laces-down on a bench, front foot a long stride ahead, hips and shoulders square.
Dumbbells at your sides; from the front, keep the front knee, ankle and foot stacked in one line.
execution: Lower under control until the back knee nearly touches the floor, letting the front knee travel forward.
Upright torso keeps it on the quads; leaning forward from the hips shifts it toward the glutes.
Drive up through the whole front foot; the back leg only balances, it should not push.
cue.feel: A deep stretch across the front thigh at the bottom, then the front leg alone bringing you up.
cue.mistake: Pushing off the back foot or bouncing off the bench robs the front leg of the work.
cue.quickCue: Front leg does all the work; back foot just balances.

cue.target: Glutes first, then quads and inner thigh
setup: Dumbbells at your sides, stand tall, pick a clear line of floor ahead.
Take a long step, roughly a metre, long enough to feel a glute stretch while staying stable.
execution: Lower under control for about two seconds until the back knee gently touches the floor.
Keep the torso rigid; a slight forward lean from the hips deepens the glute stretch.
Drive up through the front foot, then step through and set the next rep.
cue.feel: A deep stretch in the front-leg glute at the bottom and that glute pushing you up.
cue.mistake: Short, shallow steps, which turn it into a one-leg squat and shift the work onto the quads.
cue.quickCue: Long step, knee kisses the floor, drive up

cue.target: Glutes first, then quads and inner thigh
setup: Stand tall with dumbbells at your sides and enough space behind you to step back.
Step back far enough that the front shin stays near vertical at the bottom.
execution: Lower under control for two seconds until the back knee lightly touches the floor.
Keep most of your weight on the front foot; the back leg is only a kickstand.
Drive up through the front heel and return to standing before the next rep.
cue.feel: The front-leg glute stretching at the bottom and doing the pushing; the back leg contributes little.
cue.mistake: Pushing off the back foot to stand up, which takes the work away from the front-leg glute.
cue.quickCue: Weight on front foot, back leg is a kickstand

cue.target: Glutes and quads of the lead leg
setup: Use a box around knee height, whole lead foot flat on top, heel fully on.
Hold dumbbells at your sides or go bodyweight; stand tall close to the box.
execution: Lean the chest slightly forward and drive through the heel of the top foot to stand.
Keep the back foot passive; it only balances, it should not push off the floor.
Lower under control for two to three seconds until the back toes just touch down.
cue.feel: The glute and quad of the top leg doing the lifting, with a deep glute stretch at the bottom.
cue.mistake: Bouncing off the back foot to launch up, which takes most of the work off the lead leg.
cue.quickCue: Drive through the top heel, back foot stays quiet

cue.target: Quads, all four heads
setup: Set the back pad so the knees line up with the pivot, ankle pad just above the feet.
Recline the seat slightly and pull the hips down into it; do not sit bolt upright.
execution: Point the toes straight ahead so the knees track with the hips, not turned in or out.
Extend until the knees are fully straight and squeeze the quads hard at the top.
Lower under control for two to three seconds all the way down without bouncing.
cue.feel: Quads tightening hard at the top and stretching at the bottom; nothing else should be working.
cue.mistake: Swinging the weight up and letting it drop, or the hips lifting off the seat to help the rep.
cue.quickCue: Full lockout, slow lower, hips stay down.
cue.why: A knee isolation lift, so it is done strict and controlled with moderate weight; heaving heavy loads adds little quad tension and makes reps sloppy.

cue.target: Quads, especially the rectus femoris
setup: Stand tall holding a post or cable for balance, feet hip width, heels free to rise.
Squeeze the glutes and brace so the hips stay pushed forward the whole time.
execution: Lean the torso back as one straight line while the knees travel forward and heels rise.
Go as far as you can control, then pull up with the quads without bending at the hips.
Lower under control for two to three seconds; the movement gets harder the deeper you go.
cue.feel: A hard stretch and burn down the front of the thighs; hips stay locked out throughout.
cue.mistake: Folding at the hips turns it into a regular squat and takes the stretch off the quads.
cue.quickCue: Hips forward, lean back, knees travel forward.
cue.why: Done with bodyweight or light assistance because leverage makes the bottom very hard; it is a stretch-focused movement, so progress by control and depth.

cue.target: Quads, with glutes assisting
setup: Feet about shoulder width, toes turned out slightly, weight spread over the whole foot.
Arms reach forward or hands together at the chest to help balance.
execution: Sit down between the knees as deep as you can control, knees following the toes.
Chest stays up and heels stay down through the bottom of the squat.
Stand by driving the floor away until the hips and knees are straight.
cue.feel: The front of the thighs doing most of the work, glutes helping as you rise from the bottom.
cue.mistake: Knees caving inward or heels lifting, which shifts the load and costs balance and depth.
cue.quickCue: Sit between your knees, heels down
cue.why: Bodyweight is light for the legs, so slow lowering, a pause at the bottom, or a single-leg version adds difficulty.

cue.target: Quads, same pattern as a front squat, with glutes assisting
setup: Hold one dumbbell or kettlebell vertically against your chest with both hands, elbows tucked under it.
Feet shoulder width or slightly wider, toes turned out a little, weight spread over the whole foot.
execution: Sit straight down between your knees, chest high, knees pointing the same way as your toes.
Lower under control until thighs pass parallel; the front load keeps your torso upright.
Stand by driving the floor away, keeping the weight glued to your chest the whole way up.
cue.feel: Quads doing the work at the bottom and through the rise, torso stacked and steady over midfoot.
cue.mistake: Letting the weight drift away from your chest tips you forward and turns it into an arm and back exercise.
cue.quickCue: Weight on chest, sit deep, stay tall.

cue.target: Standing-leg quads and glutes, with the outer hip stabilising
setup: Stand on one foot, other leg held straight out in front, arms reaching forward as a counterweight.
Whole foot flat; holding a rail or squatting to a box are fair ways to make it easier.
execution: Sit down as far as you can under control, knee tracking over the toes, heel staying down.
Reach the arms and free leg forward as you descend so your weight stays over the foot.
Drive the floor away to stand, finishing with the hip and knee fully straight.
cue.feel: The standing quad loaded hard at the bottom with the outer hip working to keep you steady.
cue.mistake: Knee collapsing inward or the heel lifting shifts the load off the quad and costs your balance.
cue.quickCue: Heel down, knee over toes, reach forward for balance.

cue.target: Hamstrings and glutes, with lower back holding a fixed position
setup: Start standing with the bar at your thighs, shoulder-width grip, feet hip width, toes slightly out.
Soften the knees slightly and lock that bend in; chest lifted, shoulders pulled back, big breath.
execution: Push your hips straight back, letting the bar slide down your thighs, shins staying nearly vertical.
Lower under control until the hips can't go further back without rounding, usually just below the knees.
Drive the hips forward to stand tall, bar tight to the legs; don't lean back at the top.
cue.feel: A strong hamstring stretch building as the hips travel back, then hamstrings and glutes pulling you upright.
cue.mistake: Chasing depth by rounding the back or bending the knees more takes tension off the hamstrings.
cue.quickCue: Hips back, soft knees, stop before the back rounds.

cue.target: Hamstrings and glutes, with the lower back stabilising
setup: Stand tall, feet hip width, a dumbbell in each hand resting against the front of the thighs.
Soft bend in the knees, chest up, shoulder blades pulled back, and brace before every rep.
execution: Push the hips straight back and let the dumbbells slide down the thighs, weight shifting to the heels.
Keep the back flat and the knees bent the same amount until you feel a strong hamstring stretch.
Lower under control for two to three seconds, pause, then drive the hips forward and squeeze the glutes.
cue.feel: A deep pull down the back of the thighs at the bottom, then glutes finishing the lift.
cue.mistake: Letting the dumbbells drift forward away from the legs, which rounds the back and unloads the hamstrings.
cue.quickCue: Hips back, dumbbells brush the thighs.

cue.target: Hamstrings and glutes, with lower back holding a fixed position
setup: Start standing with the bar at your thighs, shoulder-width grip, feet hip width, toes slightly out.
Soften the knees slightly and lock that bend in; chest lifted, shoulders pulled back, big breath.
execution: Push your hips straight back, letting the bar slide down your thighs, shins staying nearly vertical.
Lower under control until the hips can't go further back without rounding, usually just below the knees.
Drive the hips forward to stand tall, bar tight to the legs; don't lean back at the top.
cue.feel: A strong hamstring stretch building as the hips travel back, then hamstrings and glutes pulling you upright.
cue.mistake: Chasing depth by rounding the back or bending the knees more takes tension off the hamstrings.
cue.quickCue: Hips back, soft knees, stop before the back rounds.

cue.target: Glutes and hamstrings, with lower back and quads assisting
setup: Feet hip width, bar over midfoot about an inch from your shins, hands just outside your legs.
Hips back to reach the bar, shins touching it, chest up, shoulders over the bar, big breath.
execution: Tense against the bar until it clicks, then push the floor away, bar dragging up the shins.
Hips and shoulders rise together; once the bar passes the knees, drive the hips through to stand tall.
Lower under control by pushing the hips back first, bending the knees only once the bar clears them.
cue.feel: Hamstrings and glutes loaded before the bar moves, back locked flat, bar pinned against your legs.
cue.mistake: Hips shooting up first leaves the back doing the lift; bar drifting forward off the shins does the same.
cue.quickCue: Bar tight to shins, chest up, hips through.

cue.target: Glutes, with quads and inner thighs doing more than conventional
setup: Feet wide with toes flared out, shins vertical from the front, hands inside your legs at shoulder width.
Hips back, knees pushed out over the toes to reach the bar, torso much more upright than conventional.
execution: Tense against the bar until it clicks, then spread the floor apart with your feet and be patient.
Chest up, knees out as the bar leaves the floor; once past the knees, drive the hips forward.
Lower under control: hips back first, knees out, bar sliding down the legs in a straight line.
cue.feel: Inner thighs and glutes stretched and loaded at the start, quads pushing the floor apart, back staying upright.
cue.mistake: Knees caving in or hips rising early drops the chest and turns it into a rounded conventional pull.
cue.quickCue: Spread the floor, knees out, patient off the floor.

cue.target: Glutes and hamstrings, with more quads than a straight-bar pull
setup: Stand inside the bar, feet hip to shoulder width, handles beside your midfoot.
Push hips back and down, grip the side handles palms-in, chest up, torso more upright than a barbell.
execution: Brace, tense against the handles, then push the floor away with hips and knees straightening together.
Keep the weight centred over midfoot; because the load sits beside you, knees can travel further forward.
Stand tall without leaning back, then lower under control by pushing the hips back and bending the knees.
cue.feel: Glutes and hamstrings driving the hips through, with the quads sharing the work more than usual, back steady.
cue.mistake: Hips shooting up before the handles move tips you forward and loads the lower back instead of the legs.
cue.quickCue: Stay upright, push the floor away, hips through.

cue.target: Hamstrings, with some sartorius
setup: Lie face down with the knees just off the bench edge and the pad above the heels.
Grip the handles and press the hips into the bench; on this version the hips stay extended.
execution: Curl the pad toward the glutes, keeping the hips pressed down the whole rep.
Lower under control for two to three seconds to fully straight knees.
Pause or reverse slowly at the bottom rather than bouncing into the next rep.
cue.feel: Hamstrings squeezing hard at the top; the stretch at the bottom is milder than the seated curl.
cue.mistake: Hips rising off the pad as the weight comes up, which uses the lower back and shortens the range.
cue.quickCue: Hips glued down, curl to the glutes.
cue.why: The hamstrings are less stretched here than when seated, so use it as a strict, higher-rep squeeze-focused curl rather than a heavy lift.

cue.target: Hamstrings, all heads
setup: Set the thigh pad snug and the ankle pad just above the heels, legs fully straight to start.
Sit with the hips back and torso upright or leaning slightly forward for more stretch.
execution: Curl until the pad touches the back of the thighs, keeping the hips pinned under the pad.
Lower under control for two to three seconds all the way back to straight knees.
Pause or reverse slowly at the stretched position; never bounce out of the bottom.
cue.feel: A strong stretch behind the thighs at the top of the range and a hard squeeze at the bottom.
cue.mistake: Cutting the range short at either end, or lifting the hips to yank the pad down.
cue.quickCue: Full stretch, full squeeze, no bouncing.
cue.why: Preferred over the lying curl because sitting stretches the hamstrings at the hip, which drives more growth; usually done for higher reps with strict control.

cue.target: Hamstrings, especially the short head
setup: Kneel on a pad with the ankles anchored low and firmly; hands ready in front of the chest.
Squeeze the glutes and brace so the hips stay fully extended, body straight from knees to head.
execution: Lower the torso forward as one rigid line by opening the knees only, as slowly as you can.
Fight the descent the entire way until you catch yourself with the hands.
Push back lightly with the hands and pull with the hamstrings to return, hips still extended.
cue.feel: Hamstrings straining hard against gravity and getting harder the closer you get to the floor.
cue.mistake: Bending at the hips so you sit back onto the ankles, which drops the load off the hamstrings.
cue.quickCue: Hips locked out, lower as slowly as possible.
cue.why: Bodyweight gets extremely heavy near the floor, so the exercise lives in the slow lowering phase; progress by control and depth, not added weight.

cue.target: Hamstrings, one leg at a time
setup: Set the pad above the working heel; rest the other foot on the floor or frame.
Use a lighter load than the two-leg curl and square the hips to the machine.
execution: Curl until the pad reaches the back of the thigh without letting the hip twist or lift.
Lower under control for two to three seconds to a fully straight knee.
Pause at the stretched bottom, then repeat; finish the weaker leg first, then match reps.
cue.feel: Only the working hamstring squeezing and stretching; the pelvis stays still on the pad.
cue.mistake: Rotating the hips or hiking the pelvis to help the working leg, which robs it of tension.
cue.quickCue: Hips square, one leg does all the work.
cue.why: Done lighter and strictly because one leg carries the load; it evens out a stronger side and removes the temptation to cheat with the hips.

cue.target: Hamstrings and glutes, with lower back holding position
setup: Bar on the upper back as for a squat, feet about hip to shoulder width.
Unlock the knees slightly, big breath, brace hard, squeeze the bar into your back.
