execution: Push the hips straight back and let the torso tip forward, back flat, knees fixed.
Lower under control for two to three seconds until the hamstrings are fully stretched.
Drive the hips forward to stand tall, stopping before the back rounds on the way down.
cue.feel: A deep pull through the hamstrings as you tip forward, then glutes and hamstrings bringing you up.
cue.mistake: Rounding the lower back to go deeper, or bending the knees more so it turns into a squat.
cue.quickCue: Hips back, flat back, stop at the stretch

cue.target: Hamstrings and glutes of the standing leg
setup: Stand on one leg with a soft knee, bodyweight or one dumbbell held in the hands.
Brace the abs and keep the hips square to the floor, not rotating open.
execution: Hinge at the hip, chest lowering as the free leg reaches straight back in line with the torso.
Back flat, weight in the mid-foot; go as far as the hamstring stretch allows without rounding.
Drive the hip forward to stand tall, squeezing the glute of the standing leg.
cue.feel: A strong stretch in the back of the standing thigh at the bottom, then that glute bringing you up.
cue.mistake: Opening the hips toward the ceiling or rounding the back to reach lower.
cue.quickCue: Hips square, reach the back leg long
cue.why: Balance limits the load before the hamstring does; light toe contact on the floor behind you is a fair way to steady it.

cue.target: Glutes, mainly the middle; hamstrings assist
setup: Upper back on a bench about knee height, padded bar in the crease of your hips.
Feet a bit wider than hips, toes slightly out, shins vertical at the top.
execution: Squeeze your glutes to drive the bar straight up until your hips fully lock out.
Chin tucked, eyes forward, ribs down; crunch your abs slightly so the low back stays flat.
Lower under control for about two seconds, letting the glutes stretch, then squeeze again.
cue.feel: A hard cramp-like squeeze in the glutes at lockout; the burn there tells you the hips are extended.
cue.mistake: Arching the lower back and looking up at the top, which shifts the work off the glutes.
cue.quickCue: Chin down, squeeze glutes to full lockout
cue.why: Leverage peaks at lockout, so the top squeeze is the point; chin tucked keeps the glutes, not the low back, finishing the rep.

cue.target: Glutes, mainly the middle; hamstrings assist
setup: Belt or pad snug across the hip crease; upper back and traps settled into the backrest.
Heels closer to the platform than feels natural, so you get real depth at the bottom.
execution: Drive the pad up by squeezing your glutes until the hips are fully locked out.
Hold the squeeze for a beat at the top with chin tucked and ribs down.
Lower under control for two to three seconds; the machine's stability lets you focus purely on the glutes.
cue.feel: Strongest at the top, where the machine's resistance peaks; the glutes should cramp together on every lockout.
cue.mistake: Spreading the feet far out front, which cuts range of motion and turns the rep into a top-only bounce.
cue.quickCue: Heels in, lock out, hold the squeeze
cue.why: The machine is stable and comfortable, so it is loaded heavy and progressed weekly; the top squeeze matters because tension is highest at lockout.

cue.target: Glutes of the working leg, including the upper side glute
setup: Upper back on a bench, one foot flat under the knee, the other leg lifted.
Hold the free knee to your chest; optionally rest a dumbbell on the working hip.
execution: Push through the heel of the planted foot and raise the hips until fully locked out.
Keep both hips level at the top; do not let the free side drop or twist.
Lower under control for two to three seconds, then squeeze again from the bottom.
cue.feel: A strong squeeze in the working glute at the top, plus the side of the hip working to stay level.
cue.mistake: Letting the pelvis tilt or rotate toward the free leg, or arching the lower back to finish.
cue.quickCue: Hips level, squeeze the working glute to lockout
cue.why: One leg makes it much harder, so light or bodyweight loads are normal; the balance demand also works the side glutes.

cue.target: Glutes; hamstrings assist
setup: Lie on the floor, padded bar across the hip crease, knees bent, feet flat and hip width.
Start with the hips on the floor; the shorter range is the difference from a hip thrust.
execution: Squeeze your glutes to lift the hips until the body is straight from shoulders to knees.
Chin tucked, ribs down, abs lightly braced so the hips finish without arching the back.
Pause and squeeze hard at the top, then lower under control for two seconds.
cue.feel: A short, intense squeeze in the glutes at lockout; because the range is small, every rep should end there.
cue.mistake: Pushing the hips so high the lower back arches, which takes the finish away from the glutes.
cue.quickCue: Squeeze glutes to a straight line, ribs down
cue.why: Range is shorter than a hip thrust, so the rep lives in the top squeeze; it can be loaded heavy, but only lockout counts.

cue.target: Glutes, especially the upper glute
setup: Ankle strap on a low pulley, face the stack and hold the frame for support.
Hinge forward slightly at the hips, standing knee soft, working leg just in front of you.
execution: Kick the working leg back and slightly out on a diagonal, leading with the heel.
Stop when the hip is fully extended; keep the torso still and the pelvis square.
Return under control for two to three seconds until you feel the glute stretch.
cue.feel: A squeeze high on the glute at the back of the kick, not in the lower back.
cue.mistake: Swinging the leg too high so the lower back arches and the hips rotate open to finish.
cue.quickCue: Kick back and out, torso still, no back arch
cue.why: A small isolation move, so it is done light and strict; heavier loads just recruit the lower back and swinging.

cue.target: Side glutes (glute medius and minimus), upper glute max
setup: Sit with the pads on the outside of your knees, feet on the rests, holding the handles.
Lean the torso forward from the hips, back flat, instead of sitting against the pad.
execution: Push the knees apart as wide as the machine allows, pausing briefly at the widest point.
Keep the forward lean fixed; do not rock the torso to move the pads.
Return under control for two to three seconds until the pads almost meet.
cue.feel: Deep burn in the upper outer glutes, getting stronger toward the widest point.
cue.mistake: Rocking the body back and forth or letting the pads slam together between reps.
cue.quickCue: Lean forward, push knees wide, control the return
cue.why: A small-muscle isolation lift with a short range, so it is done strict and moderately light with higher reps to keep tension on the glutes.

cue.target: Side glutes (glute medius and minimus)
setup: Ankle strap on a low pulley, stand side-on with the far leg attached.
Hold the frame with the near hand; standing knee soft, torso tall, hips level.
execution: Sweep the working leg straight out to the side, toes pointing forward, leg straight.
Only the hip moves; stop the moment your torso starts leaning away.
Lower under control for two to three seconds, letting the leg cross slightly in front.
cue.feel: A burn on the side of the hip, just below the belt line, of the working leg.
cue.mistake: Leaning away, hitching the hip, or rolling the toes up to swing higher, which lets other muscles take over.
cue.quickCue: Toes forward, torso still, sweep the leg out
cue.why: The side glutes are small and the range is short, so this is done light and strict with higher reps rather than heavy.

cue.target: Inner thighs (adductors)
setup: Set the pads open to a stretch you can control, pads on the inside of the knees.
Sit tall with your lower back against the pad, feet on the rests, holding the handles.
execution: Squeeze the thighs together until the pads meet, driving through the knees.
Keep the lower back against the pad; do not arch to open the hips wider.
Let the pads open under control for two to three seconds back to the start width.
cue.feel: A stretch along the inner thighs as the pads open, then a firm squeeze as they close.
cue.mistake: Letting the pads fly open and bouncing out of the stretch, or slamming them together at the finish.
cue.quickCue: Back on the pad, squeeze together, slow open

cue.target: Glutes and hamstrings, with the lower back assisting
setup: Lie face down with the hip crease at the edge of the pad, legs hanging down.
Grip the handles with straight arms so the upper body stays pinned.
execution: Squeeze the glutes to lift straight legs until they reach about torso height.
Pause briefly at the top; going much higher just arches the lower back.
Lower under control for two to three seconds until the legs hang below the pad.
cue.feel: The glutes and hamstrings lifting the legs, and lengthening as the legs hang below the pad.
cue.mistake: Flinging the legs up with momentum and arching past level, which moves the work into the lower back.
cue.quickCue: Squeeze glutes up to level, control it down

cue.target: Glutes, with hamstrings assisting
setup: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat on the floor about hip width.
Arms on the floor by your sides; tuck the pelvis slightly to set the glutes.
execution: Squeeze the glutes to lift the hips until shoulders, hips and knees form a straight line.
Ribs down and chin tucked so the hips finish without arching the lower back.
Pause and squeeze at the top, then lower under control to the floor.
cue.feel: A strong squeeze in the glutes at the top; hamstrings help, but the lower back should stay quiet.
cue.mistake: Pushing the hips so high the lower back arches, taking the finish away from the glutes.
cue.quickCue: Squeeze glutes to a straight line, ribs down
cue.why: Bodyweight is light for the glutes, so a pause at the top or a single-leg version adds difficulty.

cue.target: Calves, mainly the gastrocnemius (the visible upper diamond)
setup: Balls of the feet on the edge of the step, heels free to drop below it.
Feet pointing straight ahead or slightly flared; flex the quads so the knees stay locked.
execution: Lower under control for two to three seconds until the heels are as low as they go.
Pause at the bottom for a full one-two count so the tendon cannot bounce you up.
Press the balls of the feet down and rise as high as possible, squeezing at the top.
cue.feel: A pulling stretch through the whole calf at the bottom, then a hard cramp at the top.
cue.mistake: Bouncing out of the bottom, which lets the Achilles tendon do the work instead of the muscle.
cue.quickCue: Full stretch, pause at the bottom, no bounce
cue.why: The tendon stores energy, so bouncing wastes reps; a slow lower, a pause at the bottom and higher reps keep the calf muscle itself working.

cue.target: Soleus, the deeper calf muscle under the gastrocnemius
setup: Balls of the feet on the platform, pad snug across the lower thighs, knees bent about ninety degrees.
The bent knee is the point: it slackens the gastrocnemius so the soleus does the work.
execution: Lower under control for two to three seconds until the heels are fully dropped.
Pause at the bottom for a one-two count, then press the balls of the feet down.
Rise as high as you can and squeeze; keep the hips and hands out of it.
cue.feel: A deep stretch low in the calf near the Achilles, and a burn there at the top.
cue.mistake: Pulling on the handles or rocking the hips to help, which turns the rep into a bounce.
cue.quickCue: Heels all the way down, pause, then press
cue.why: Bending the knee takes the visible upper calf out, so this is soleus-only; it responds to lighter loads, higher reps and a strict pause.

cue.target: Calves, mainly the gastrocnemius (the visible upper diamond)
setup: Balls of the feet on the edge of the step, heels free to drop below it.
Feet pointing straight ahead or slightly flared; flex the quads so the knees stay locked.
execution: Lower under control for two to three seconds until the heels are as low as they go.
Pause at the bottom for a full one-two count so the tendon cannot bounce you up.
Press the balls of the feet down and rise as high as possible, squeezing at the top.
cue.feel: A pulling stretch through the whole calf at the bottom, then a hard cramp at the top.
cue.mistake: Bouncing out of the bottom, which lets the Achilles tendon do the work instead of the muscle.
cue.quickCue: Full stretch, pause at the bottom, no bounce
cue.why: The tendon stores energy, so bouncing wastes reps; a slow lower, a pause at the bottom and higher reps keep the calf muscle itself working.

cue.target: Calves, mainly the gastrocnemius; knees stay straight
setup: Balls of the feet on the bottom edge of the platform, heels hanging off.
Press the sled to straight legs and keep the knees locked; do not bend them to help.
execution: Let the platform push your toes back for two to three seconds into a full stretch.
Pause at the bottom for a one-two count so nothing rebounds.
Press through the balls of the feet to full point, squeeze, then lower again.
cue.feel: A strong stretch through the calf at the bottom, with the knees locked and the calf alone moving.
cue.mistake: Bending the knees or letting the feet slip lower on the platform, which cuts the stretch.
cue.quickCue: Knees locked, toes back to full stretch, pause
cue.why: The sled is stable, so it is loaded heavier than most calf raises; the deep stretched half of the rep is where growth comes from.

cue.target: One calf at a time, mainly the gastrocnemius
setup: Ball of one foot on the edge of a step, dumbbell in the same-side hand.
Other hand holds a rail; keep the working knee straight by flexing the quad.
execution: Lower under control for two to three seconds until the heel drops as far as possible.
Pause at the bottom for a one-two count, then press the ball of the foot down.
Rise to a full point on the ball of the foot, squeeze, and lower again.
cue.feel: A deep stretch in that single calf at the bottom and a cramp at the top; no wobble.
cue.mistake: Letting go of the support so balance, not the calf, limits the set; or bending the knee.
cue.quickCue: Hold the rail, full stretch, pause, press
cue.why: One leg means the load is lighter and the reps higher; holding on is not cheating, stability is what lets the calf work hard.

cue.target: One calf at a time, mainly the gastrocnemius
setup: Ball of one foot on the edge of a step, heel hanging off, other foot lifted.
Hold a rail or wall for balance; keep the working knee straight.
execution: Lower under control until the heel drops as far as it can, and pause in the stretch.
Press through the ball of the foot and rise as high as possible.
Squeeze briefly at the top, then lower slowly again without bouncing.
cue.feel: A deep stretch in the calf at the bottom and a hard squeeze at the top.
cue.mistake: Bouncing out of the bottom or cutting the range short at either end.
cue.quickCue: Hold the rail, full stretch, pause, rise high
cue.why: The step lets the heel drop below the toes for a longer range; holding on keeps balance from limiting the calf.

cue.target: Abs (rectus abdominis), upper portion emphasised
setup: Kneel facing a high pulley, rope held at the sides of your head, hands loose.
Squeeze the glutes to tuck the pelvis under before the first rep.
execution: Crunch the ribs down and in toward the pelvis, rounding the lower back on purpose.
Hips stay put, arms are hooks; return for two to three seconds to a tall spine.
cue.feel: A hard contraction along the whole front of the abdomen, strongest as the spine rounds fully.
cue.mistake: Pulling the rope down with the arms or folding at the hips, which moves the weight without bending the spine.
cue.quickCue: Round the spine down and in; hips stay still.
cue.why: Moderate load, full range: rounding the spine under a cable is what the abs do; controlled reps beat piling on weight the hips lift.

cue.target: Abs, lower portion emphasised, with hip flexors assisting
setup: Hang from a bar, grip a bit wider than shoulders; use straps if grip gives out first.
Start from a dead hang, legs straight, body still.
execution: Begin by rolling the hips forward and up, curling the lower abs toward the ribs.
Bring the legs up until the hips are fully curled, then lower for two to three seconds.
Finish each rep at a still dead hang; no swinging into the next one.
cue.feel: The lower abs shorten as the pelvis curls; the legs are just the load hanging off it.
cue.mistake: Lifting the legs with the pelvis fixed, which is hip flexor work and gets easy fast.
cue.quickCue: Curl the hips up, not just the legs.
cue.why: Abs grow like any muscle: from load and control. Curling the pelvis and lowering slowly beats fast reps that only train the hip flexors.

cue.target: Abs, lower portion emphasised, with hip flexors assisting
setup: Forearms on the pads, back pressed into the pad, hold the handles lightly.
The pad kills swinging, so this is the place to learn the hip curl.
execution: Roll the pelvis up and forward first, then let the knees or straight legs rise with it.
Lower for two to three seconds until the pelvis returns to neutral, back still on the pad.
cue.feel: The lower abs shorten and the lower back rounds slightly off the pad at the top.
cue.mistake: Lifting the knees with the back flat on the pad; the abs never shorten, hip flexors do it all.
cue.quickCue: Back on the pad, curl the pelvis, not the knees.
cue.why: Without the swing the abs must do everything, so reps are slower and fewer; progress by straightening the legs, not by speeding up.

cue.target: Abs and obliques, resisting spinal extension
setup: Kneel with the wheel under your shoulders, glutes squeezed so the pelvis is tucked under.
Brace as if about to take a punch before the wheel moves.
execution: Roll out slowly, letting the wheel travel only as far as the lower back stays flat.
Pull back by crunching the abs; the arms simply follow the wheel in.
Take two to three seconds each way, hips never sagging toward the floor.
cue.feel: Think of it as a moving plank: the abs burn hardest at the far point holding the back flat.
cue.mistake: Letting the lower back arch and hips sag at the far point, or dragging the wheel back with the arms.
cue.quickCue: Only as far as the back stays flat.
cue.why: Progress by rolling further, not by more reps: a longer reach with a flat back is a heavier load for the abs.

cue.target: Abs (rectus abdominis), upper portion emphasised
setup: Hook your feet under the pads and lie back until the abs are fully stretched.
Hands lightly at the temples or across the chest, chin slightly tucked.
execution: Curl the ribs toward the pelvis, rounding the lower back off the bench, rather than sitting up straight.
Squeeze, then lower for two to three seconds until the abs stretch again at the bottom.
Hold a plate on the chest to add load once bodyweight gets easy.
cue.feel: A strong contraction across the front of the abs, biggest when the spine is fully rounded.
cue.mistake: Sitting up with a flat back, which turns it into a hip flexor exercise and the decline makes that worse.
cue.quickCue: Round the spine; don't sit up flat.
cue.why: The decline lets you stretch the abs fully and add a plate later; abs grow from loaded, full-range reps, not from fast half-reps.

cue.target: Abs, obliques and deep core, resisting spinal extension
setup: Elbows directly under the shoulders, up on the toes, body a straight line from head to heels.
Squeeze the glutes to tuck the pelvis under before you start the clock.
execution: Pull elbows toward toes and toes toward elbows; nothing moves, but the abs tighten hard.
Breathe normally without letting the brace go.
Hold until the line breaks; when it gets easy, move the elbows forward toward eye level.
cue.feel: The abs and glutes work the whole hold; the lower back stays quiet.
cue.mistake: Hips piked up or sagging down; both take the abs out of it. Squeeze the glutes to fix either.
cue.quickCue: Glutes tight, pelvis tucked, straight line.
cue.why: Progress by making the hold harder, not longer: a tucked pelvis and elbows further forward load the abs more than another minute of easy holding.

cue.target: Abs, lower portion emphasised, with hip flexors assisting
setup: Lie on your back, hands at your sides or gripping a bench behind your head.
Bend hips and knees to a right angle, lower back flat against the floor.
execution: Curl the hips off the floor, rolling the pelvis up toward the ribs.
Knees drift toward the chest; the lift comes from the hip curl, not a leg kick.
Lower one vertebra at a time for two to three seconds until the hips touch down.
cue.feel: The lower abs shorten as the tailbone lifts; the hip flexors should feel secondary.
cue.mistake: Swinging the legs up and back with momentum, so the hips flex but the pelvis never curls.
cue.quickCue: Curl the tailbone up toward the ribs.
cue.why: Abs respond to control, not speed: a slow full curl of the pelvis beats fast reps that only swing the legs.

cue.target: Glutes and hamstrings, with the lower back assisting
setup: Set the pad just below the hip crease so you can fold forward freely at the hips.
Feet flat on the platform, arms crossed on the chest or holding a plate.
execution: Lower under control for two to three seconds, folding at the hips as low as you can.
Drive your hips into the pad and squeeze the glutes to raise the torso.
Stop when the body forms a straight line; do not lean back past it.
cue.feel: A stretch in the glutes and hamstrings at the bottom, then a hard glute squeeze at the top.
cue.mistake: Pad set too high so the hips cannot bend, turning it into a lower back movement.
cue.quickCue: Hips into the pad, squeeze glutes, stop straight

cue.target: Front of the neck, the muscles that tuck your chin to chest
setup: Lie on your back on a bench with your head and neck just past the end.
Hold a light plate on your forehead over a folded towel, both hands steadying it.
execution: Let your head lower back gently, then tuck the chin and curl it toward your chest.
Hands only keep the plate in place; the neck does all the lifting.
Lower under control for two to three seconds; keep shoulders flat on the bench.
cue.feel: Work along the front and sides of the neck, strongest as the chin comes toward the chest.
cue.mistake: Lifting the shoulders off the bench or pushing with the arms, turning it into a crunch.
cue.quickCue: Tuck the chin, curl slowly, arms only steady.
cue.why: Neck flexion is weaker than extension, so this uses a lighter plate; smooth, strict reps keep the work in the neck.

cue.target: Neck extensors at the back of the neck, with upper traps assisting
setup: Lie face down on a bench with your head and neck just past the end.
Hold a plate on the back of your head over a folded towel, using both hands.
execution: Let your chin drop toward the floor, then lift your head until looking straight ahead.
Hands only keep the plate in place; the neck does all the lifting.
Lower under control for two to three seconds; keep the chest on the bench.
cue.feel: A building burn along the back of the neck, with a gentle stretch as the chin lowers.
cue.mistake: Pushing the plate up with your arms or arching the upper back, which takes the neck out of it.
cue.quickCue: Hands just hold the plate; neck does the lifting.
cue.why: Kept light and strict: the neck muscles are small, so smooth, controlled reps with modest plates beat heavy, jerky ones.

cue.target: Front of the neck, the muscles that tuck your chin down
setup: Lie face-up on a flat bench, shoulders at the end, head and neck hanging free.
Fit the harness snug with the plate hanging from the front strap, below your head.
execution: Tuck your chin first, then curl your head up toward your chest.
Keep your shoulders flat on the bench; only the neck moves.
Lower under control for two to three seconds, just past level into a gentle stretch.
cue.feel: Work along the front and sides of the neck, with the chin tuck doing the lifting.
cue.mistake: Lifting your shoulders off the bench or pulling the chain with your hands to help the neck.
cue.quickCue: Chin tucked, shoulders down, curl your head up.
cue.why: Loaded lighter than neck extension because the front of the neck is weaker; smooth, strict reps load it better than heavy, jerky ones.

cue.target: Neck extensors at the back of the neck, with upper traps assisting
setup: Fit the harness snug so it stays put when you shake your head.
Hinge forward with hands on your thighs or a bench, torso still, plate hanging freely.
execution: Let the plate lower your chin toward your chest, stopping just short of a full stretch.
Lift your head until you look straight ahead, moving only at the neck.
Lower under control for two to three seconds; never let the plate drop or bounce.
cue.feel: A steady burn in the back of the neck and upper traps, smooth through the whole range.
cue.mistake: Jerking the head up or bobbing the torso to swing the plate, instead of moving smoothly from the neck.
cue.quickCue: Slow and smooth; move only your head.
cue.why: Kept light and progressed slowly: the neck muscles are small, and smooth, strict reps load them better than heavy, jerky ones.

cue.target: Wrist and finger flexors on the palm side of the forearm
setup: Sit with forearms on your thighs or a bench, wrists just past the edge, palms up.
Grip the bar with both hands about hip-width apart; forearms stay pinned throughout.
execution: Let the bar roll down toward your fingertips, opening the hand as the wrist bends back.
Close the fist, then curl the wrist up as high as it goes.
Lower under control for two to three seconds; only the hands move.
cue.feel: A deep burn through the inner forearm, with a stretch at the bottom as the bar reaches the fingers.
cue.mistake: Cutting the range short at the bottom to move more weight, which skips the stretched half of the rep.
cue.quickCue: Roll to the fingertips, then curl all the way up.
cue.why: Forearm flexors are small and respond well to lighter, higher-rep work; full range matters more than the load on the bar.

cue.target: Wrist and finger flexors, one forearm at a time
setup: Kneel or sit beside a bench, forearm flat on it, wrist just past the edge, palm up.
Hold one dumbbell, with your free hand pressing the working forearm down.
execution: Let the dumbbell roll toward your fingertips, then close the fist and curl the wrist up.
Keep the handle level; do not let the wrist twist or tilt sideways.
Lower under control for two to three seconds to a full stretch.
cue.feel: A focused burn in one inner forearm, with a clear stretch each time the dumbbell rolls into the fingers.
cue.mistake: Lifting the forearm off the bench to help the weight up, which takes the wrist out of it.
cue.quickCue: Forearm pinned, roll to the fingers, curl fully.
cue.why: Kept light with full range: the forearm flexors are small and grow well from lighter, higher-rep work, not heavy partial reps.

cue.target: Wrist extensors on the back of the forearm
setup: Sit with forearms flat on your thighs or a bench, wrists past the edge, palms down.
Hold the bar or dumbbells with noticeably less weight than a regular wrist curl.
execution: Let the knuckles drop toward the floor, then lift the back of the hand up high.
Keep forearms flat and still; only the wrists move.
Lower under control for two to three seconds to a full stretch.
cue.feel: A burn across the top of the forearm, just below the elbow, building as the set goes on.
cue.mistake: Lifting the forearms or rocking the body to raise the weight, so the wrist extensors barely work.
cue.quickCue: Forearms flat, knuckles up, lower slow.
cue.why: Wrist extensors are much weaker than the flexors, so this lift uses light loads and strict, full-range reps to stay on target.

cue.target: Grip and forearms, traps, and the trunk muscles that hold you upright
setup: Stand between the weights, then pick them up like a deadlift: hips back, flat back, stand tall.
Grip the handles in the center with dry or chalked hands, shoulders pulled down and back.
execution: Brace your trunk and walk with short, steady, controlled steps, eyes fixed ahead.
Stay tall; do not lean forward or tip toward either side.
Set the weights down under control, hinging the same way you lifted them.
cue.feel: Hands and forearms burning, traps working to hold the shoulders down, trunk tight to keep you upright.
cue.mistake: Looking down and leaning forward as grip fades, letting the shoulders round and the upper back collapse.
cue.quickCue: Stand tall, shoulders down, short steady steps.

cue.target: Obliques and deep abs, resisting the cable's pull to twist
setup: Stand side-on to a chest-height cable, handle held at your sternum with both hands.
Step out until the cable pulls hard; feet hip-width, knees soft, ribs down.
execution: Press the handle straight out from your chest without letting the torso turn toward the stack.
Pause with arms long for a breath, hips and shoulders still square to the front.
Bring the handle back to the chest under control for two to three seconds.
cue.feel: Both sides of the waist brace hard to stop the twist, peaking when the arms are fully extended.
cue.mistake: Letting the hands drift toward the stack or the hips rotate, which lets the cable win the rep.
cue.quickCue: Press straight out; nothing turns toward the cable.
cue.why: Kept moderate and strict: the job is refusing to twist, so a weight that turns you only trains the cable winning.

cue.target: Obliques, resisting sideways bending of the trunk
setup: Lie on one side, elbow directly under the shoulder, forearm pointing forward, feet stacked.
Lift the hips until the body is a straight line from head to feet, top arm reaching up.
execution: Push the hips up and slightly forward so they sit in line, not dropping back or sagging down.
Brace and breathe normally; hold until the hips start to drop, then switch sides.
The plank turned sideways: the bottom-side obliques do the work instead of the abs.
cue.feel: The side of the waist nearest the floor works hard to keep the hips up; nothing else strains.
cue.mistake: Hips sinking toward the floor or rolling backward, which shifts the work off the obliques.
cue.quickCue: Hips up and forward, straight line, hold.
cue.why: Progress by making it harder, not longer: stack the feet, reach the top arm up; a long easy hold trains patience more than obliques.

cue.target: Obliques, rotating the trunk against a cable
setup: Set the pulley high, stand side-on, and grip the handle with both hands above the near shoulder.
Feet wide, knees soft, arms long and nearly straight.
execution: Rotate the ribs down and across, pulling the handle diagonally to the outside of the far hip.
Arms stay long and move with the chest; let the back heel lift so the hips turn too.
Let the handle return along the same line for two to three seconds.
cue.feel: The obliques wind up like a spring and shorten as the chest turns away from the stack.
cue.mistake: Yanking the handle down with the arms while the torso stays square, which turns it into a pulldown.
cue.quickCue: Turn the chest; arms just carry the handle.
cue.why: Moderate load and smooth reps: the obliques must turn the trunk, and heavy weight gets moved by arms and momentum instead.

cue.target: Obliques, rotating the trunk while the abs hold you leaned back
setup: Sit with knees bent, heels down, and lean back until the abs switch on, back straight.
Hold a light weight at chest height with both hands.
execution: Turn the shoulders to one side, bringing the weight toward that hip; keep the hips still.
Rotate back through the middle under control, then turn to the other side.
Rotate over two to three seconds each way, stopping short of your full twist.
cue.feel: The sides of the waist tighten on each turn while the front of the abs holds the lean.
cue.mistake: Swinging the weight side to side with the arms while the chest stays facing forward.
cue.quickCue: Turn the chest, not just the hands.
cue.why: Kept light and slow: the twist should come from the trunk, and a heavy weight turns it into momentum and arm swinging.

cue.target: Obliques, bending the trunk sideways against a load
setup: Hold one dumbbell, or a low cable handle standing side-on, arm long, feet hip-width.
Place the free hand on your hip or behind your head.
execution: Lean toward the weight until you feel a mild stretch in the opposite side.
Pull back up and a little past upright, bending away with the side opposite the weight.
Move slowly both ways, hips still, lowering for two to three seconds.
cue.feel: The side of the waist opposite the weight stretches on the way down and contracts hard to pull you up.
cue.mistake: Leaning forward, twisting, or swaying the hips to reach lower, which takes the work off the obliques.
cue.quickCue: Bend straight sideways; pull up with the far side.
cue.why: Moderate weight and a strict sideways path: heavy loads get dragged up by leaning or twisting, which leaves the obliques short of work.

cue.target: Front of the shin (tibialis anterior)
setup: Lean your back against a wall, feet about a foot out, heels on the floor.
Keep your legs straight; setting your feet farther out makes each rep harder.
execution: Pull your toes up toward your shins as high as they go, heels staying down.
Squeeze the top for a moment with the shins fully tight.
Lower the toes under control for two to three seconds until they touch down lightly.
cue.feel: A growing burn along the front of the shins and tops of the feet.
cue.mistake: Bending the knees or bouncing the toes off the floor, using momentum instead of lifting with the shins.
cue.quickCue: Heels down, toes to shins, slow lower
cue.why: A small muscle with a short range, so it is done with bodyweight or light load and higher reps until the shins burn.

cue.target: Front of the shin (tibialis anterior)
setup: Sit on a tall bench or box, lower legs hanging, feet clear of the floor.
Slide both feet into the tib bar with the pads snug over the tops of your feet.
execution: Pull your toes up toward your shins, bending only at the ankles, to lift the bar.
Squeeze briefly at the top while your thighs and knees stay still.
Lower under control for two to three seconds, letting the bar point your toes down fully.
cue.feel: The front of the shins working hard, with a stretch across the tops of the feet at the bottom.
cue.mistake: Swinging the legs or kicking from the knees to move the bar, instead of lifting it with the ankles.
cue.quickCue: Ankles only, full range, slow lower
cue.why: The bar lets you progress past bodyweight, but the muscle is small, so the load stays modest and strict with a full range.

cue.target: Serratus anterior, the muscle along your ribs under the armpit
setup: Lie on your back on a bench or the floor, dumbbells held straight up over your shoulders.
Lock the elbows; your arms stay straight for the whole set.
execution: Punch the dumbbells toward the ceiling by lifting your shoulder blades off the bench.
Keep the arms vertical and elbows straight; the reach comes only from the shoulders.
Lower for two to three seconds, letting the blades settle back flat against the bench.
cue.feel: A reaching squeeze along the sides of your ribs as your shoulders lift off the bench.
cue.mistake: Bending and pressing with the elbows, which turns it into a light bench press.
cue.quickCue: Arms locked, reach your fists to the ceiling.
cue.why: The shoulder blade travels only a short way, so light, slow reps with a full reach train the serratus better than heavy weight.

cue.target: Serratus anterior, the muscle wrapping the ribs under your armpit
setup: Get into a high plank, hands under your shoulders, body straight from head to heels.
Lock the elbows and keep them locked; only the shoulder blades will move.
execution: Let your chest sink between your hands as the shoulder blades slide together.
Push the floor away until the blades spread wide and your upper back rounds slightly.
Take two to three seconds to sink, then pause briefly at the top.
cue.feel: Work along the sides of your ribs under the armpits as you push to the top.
cue.mistake: Bending the elbows so it becomes a tiny push-up, or letting the hips sag.
cue.quickCue: Elbows locked, push the floor away, spread the blades.
cue.why: The movement is small and the muscle is hard to feel, so slow, controlled reps with a full spread matter more than adding load.
